atulshukla84340@gmail.com Concept notes covering IT Governance, IT Acts & Compliance, and Disaster Recovery & Business 
Continuity. Tight, high-yield, exam-oriented. 1. IT Governance ▬ What it is IT Governance is the framework of processes, structures, and accountability that ensures IT 
investments align with business goals and deliver value while controlling risk. It answers: Is IT doing 
the right things, and doing them well? Ownership sits with the board / senior management, not just the 
IT department. Core objectives: strategic alignment (IT ↔ business), value delivery, risk management, resource 
management, and performance measurement. ▬ Governance vs Management THE VICTORY KEY THE VICTORY KEY atulshukla84340@gmail.com Verified Student atulshukla84340@gmail.com Verifie ● Governance = sets direction, defines objectives, monitors, holds accountable ("what should be 
done" / oversight). Board-level. ● Management = plans, builds, runs, monitors operations to achieve those objectives ("how it gets 
done"). Executive-level.

● COBIT explicitly separates the two: governance (Evaluate, Direct, Monitor) sits above management. ORY KEY 4340@gmail.com Verified Student THE VICTORY KEY atulshukla84340@gmail.com Verified Student Figure 1 Governance vs management ▬ Frameworks @gmail.com Verified Student

atulshukla84340@gmail.com ▬ Indian bodies you must be able to place ▬ RBI Cyber Security Framework (2016) — banking-specific Applies to all scheduled commercial banks. Core requirements: ● A board-approved cyber security policy, distinct from the general IT policy. ● A Cyber Crisis Management Plan (CCMP) covering detection, response, recovery and containment. ● Reporting of all unusual cyber security incidents to RBI within 2–6 hours. ● Continuous surveillance — many banks run a SOC (Security Operations Centre). ● Arrangements proportionate to the bank's risk, with gap assessment against baseline controls. ORY KEY ▬ IS Audit — the essentials 4340@gmail.com Verified Student THE VICTORY KEY ● Information Systems audit independently evaluates IT controls, data integrity and compliance. ● Internal audit reports to management/the audit committee; external/statutory audit is independent 
of the organisation. ● CAAT (Computer Assisted Audit Techniques) — software used to test large data populations 
rather than samples.

● Audit trail / log = a chronological record of who did what and when — the primary evidence of 
accountability and non-repudiation. ▬ MIS (supporting concept) A Management Information System (MIS) turns data into information for managerial decisions. Its 
components are all of: data, people, hardware & software, and business procedures — a system, not 
just software. @gmail.com Verified Student

atulshukla84340@gmail.com 2. IT Acts & Compliance ▬ Information Technology Act, 2000 (India) India's primary cyber law. Purpose: ● Grant legal recognition to electronic records and e-transactions (e-commerce, e-governance). ● Give legal validity to digital/electronic signatures for authenticating records. ● Provide a legal framework to address cybercrime and prescribe penalties. ● Enable electronic filing/record-keeping with government agencies. Institutions created: Controller of Certifying Authorities (CCA) — licenses Certifying Authorities that 
issue Digital Signature Certificates; and the Cyber Appellate framework (adjudicating officers / 
appellate tribunal). THE VICTORY KEY THE VICTORY KEY ▬ 2008 Amendment atulshukla84340@gmail.com Verified Student atulshukla84340@gmail.com Verifie Strengthened and broadened the Act: ● Made it technology-neutral — recognized electronic signatures (not only "digital signatures"). ● Added/expanded offences: identity theft, cheating by impersonation, cyber terrorism, violation of 
privacy, transmitting obscene/sexually explicit material.

● Section 43A — compensation for a body corporate's failure to protect sensitive personal data 
(reasonable security practices). ● Section 66A (offensive messages) — later struck down by the Supreme Court (Shreya Singhal, 
2015) as unconstitutional. ● Section 69 — powers to intercept/monitor/decrypt; Section 70 — protected systems. Illustrative offences: Sec 65 (tampering with source documents), Sec 66 (computer-related 
offences/hacking), Sec 66C (identity theft), Sec 66D (cheating by personation), Sec 67 (obscene 
content). ORY KEY 4340@gmail.com Verified Student THE VICTORY KEY atulshukla84340@gmail.com Verified Student @gmail.com Verified Student

Higher = more reliable. ● MTTF — Mean Time To Failure: average lifespan of a non-repairable component (used once, then 
replaced). ● MTTR — Mean Time To Repair/Recover: average time to fix and restore after a failure. Lower = 
better. ● Relationship: MTBF = MTTF + MTTR (for repairable items); Availability = MTBF / (MTBF + MTTR). @gmail.com Verified Student
